name: Dispatcharr Stream Sort
description: Analyzes stream health, quality, delivery performance, and runtime reliability telemetry with M3U connection-capacity reservations, reuses fresh Dispatcharr playback metadata, then scores and reorders streams already assigned to channels.
author: matrix2669

fields.label: Sorting model
fields.description: Known-dead/stale streams are demoted below all usable streams before resolution is considered. Resolution remains a hard tier among streams with the same viability; bitrate, frame rate, M3U source, name rules, and delivery throughput score streams inside a tier.

fields.label: Channel scope
fields.description: Optional group/profile filters limit Analyze, Dry Run, Sort, and Analyze + Sort. Multiple values inside one filter are ORed; when both filters are set, a channel must match both.

fields.label: Channel group filter
fields.help_text: Optional exact Dispatcharr channel group names or IDs, separated by commas or new lines. Examples: Local, id:4. Empty means all groups. Uses the channel's effective group, including overrides.

fields.label: Channel profile filter
fields.help_text: Optional exact Dispatcharr channel profile names or IDs, separated by commas or new lines. Only enabled profile memberships are included. Empty means all profiles/channels.

fields.label: M3U source scores
fields.help_text: Legacy fallback. When the plugin is enabled this is replaced by one numeric score box per operator-managed M3U account. Locked Dispatcharr system accounts are excluded.

fields.label: Stream name scoring rules
fields.default:
# Prefix=score. Prefix rules are case-insensitive and anchored to the start of the stream name.
US=20
GO=10
TUBI=0
PRIME=-10
ROKU=-20
fields.help_text: PREFIX=score creates a case-insensitive anchored prefix rule. Advanced regex uses score::regex. All matching name rules are additive.

fields.label: Built-in incremental stream analyzer
fields.description: Analyze Streams calculates three independent due decisions at scan start: direct FFprobe statistics/reachability, grouped black/frozen/silent content validation, and throughput. Clean Dispatcharr playback can satisfy content and sustained-throughput evidence when its stream ID and M3U provider match; profile credentials are intentionally ignored. Playback never resets the direct FFprobe TTL. The analyzer preserves viewer capacity across all active M3U profiles.

fields.label: FFprobe statistics TTL (hours)
fields.help_text: Only a completed direct FFprobe resets this TTL. It refreshes reachability, resolution, FPS, codecs, and bitrate. Dispatcharr playback and stream_stats may enrich evidence but do not reset this clock. 0 forces FFprobe on every Analyze run.

fields.label: Media stability and minimum bitrate
fields.description: Resolution changes trigger throughput immediately. FPS and percentage-based bitrate changes require two consecutive direct FFprobe observations outside the rolling seven-scan baseline. Video below the configured minimum is a retryable dead result.

fields.label: Media bitrate relative tolerance (%)
fields.help_text: Bitrate changes at or below this percentage of the previous bitrate are ignored when resolution and FPS are unchanged.

fields.label: Minimum video bitrate (kbps)
fields.help_text: A direct FFprobe result below this floor is provisionally dead and enters the same immediate retry passes as other media failures. Missing bitrate does not fail this rule.

fields.label: Dead stream TTL (hours)
fields.help_text: Base exact TTL after retries confirm a stream dead. Non-placeholder failures use 1x for the first two consecutive dead results, 4x for results three through five, and 12x thereafter. Placeholder files always use the exact base TTL. Set to 0 to check confirmed-dead streams on every Analyze run.

fields.label: Scheduled analyze cron
fields.help_text: Use standard 5-field UTC cron (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, e.g. */30 * * * *). Sunday may be 0 or 7. Day-of-month and day-of-week use standard OR behavior when both are restricted. Workers poll frequently but atomically claim each due minute only once.

fields.label: Apply sort after scheduled analysis
fields.help_text: Apply Stream Sort after the scheduled Analyze scope. When enabled, scheduling keeps channel order sorted after each scan.

fields.label: Allow parallel checks on scheduled scan
fields.help_text: When enabled, scheduled scans use the configured Parallel tests value. When disabled, scheduled scans use exactly one check at a time.

fields.label: Reuse Dispatcharr playback evidence
fields.help_text: Use clean playback only when stream ID and M3U provider match. Different profiles and credentials under that provider are equivalent. Playback never resets the direct FFprobe TTL.

fields.label: Minimum playback for content (seconds)
fields.help_text: A clean unswitched playback session of at least this duration satisfies grouped black/frozen/silent content_due evidence. This is assumed content quality, not direct frame/audio detection.

fields.label: Minimum playback for throughput (seconds)
fields.help_text: A clean unswitched playback session must last at least this long before its sustained byte rate can reset throughput TTL.

fields.label: Content validation TTL (hours)
fields.help_text: Grouped black-video, frozen-video, and silent-audio evidence is reused until this TTL expires. Qualifying clean Dispatcharr playback resets this clock. If every enabled detector is inapplicable, the decision is completed without opening a provider connection.

fields.label: TTL jitter percent
fields.help_text: Apply stable per-stream analysis TTL jitter from -30% to +30% around each configured media and throughput TTL. Dead-stream TTL is never jittered.

fields.label: Healthy throughput TTL (hours)
fields.help_text: Healthy direct throughput or at least 1.10x sustained clean Dispatcharr playback is reused until this jittered TTL expires.

fields.label: Marginal/insufficient throughput TTL (hours)
fields.help_text: Marginal and insufficient throughput evidence is reused until this jittered TTL expires instead of being rechecked on the next hourly scan.

fields.label: Unknown throughput TTL (hours)
fields.help_text: Unknown throughput measurements use this shorter jittered TTL because they may represent an inconclusive provider check.

fields.label: Parallel tests
fields.help_text: Total concurrent media and throughput tests (maximum 16). Active slots are balanced across M3U sources and all active profiles, capped by each profile's remaining Dispatcharr connection-pool capacity after active viewers.

fields.label: FFprobe sample duration (seconds)
fields.help_text: Packet sample used for bitrate and metadata analysis.

fields.label: Retries for provisional failures
fields.help_text: Retries transient transport failures, invalid media, low bitrate, newly detected or inconclusive placeholders, and content failures after the first pass. A one-second recheck that confirms a previously known placeholder is terminal without retries. Retry passes use at most one simultaneous recheck per M3U source.

fields.label: Per-source analysis start delay (seconds)
fields.help_text: Minimum delay between starting media checks against the same M3U account.

fields.label: Detect fixed-duration placeholder files
fields.help_text: A continuous live stream normally has no fixed container duration. Newly detected or inconclusive placeholders use normal full-probe retries. A known placeholder is rechecked with a one-second gate at its Dead stream TTL; confirmation is terminal and skips content and throughput work.

fields.label: Detect silent audio
fields.help_text: Only applies when an audio track exists.

fields.label: Content-check sample duration (seconds)
fields.help_text: Black/frozen/silent checks share one FFmpeg decode pass.

fields.label: Integrated delivery throughput
fields.description: Throughput is part of Analyze Streams. Healthy, marginal/insufficient, and unknown evidence use their separate jittered TTL settings. Confirmed-dead streams put FFprobe, content, and throughput behind the exact adaptive dead-TTL recovery gate.

fields.label: Per-source throughput start delay (seconds)
fields.help_text: Minimum spacing between throughput starts against the same M3U source. Different sources may start at the same time, up to the Parallel tests limit.

fields.label: Runtime reliability telemetry
fields.description: Stream Sort collects runtime events and applies a bounded soft reliability score after at least 30 minutes of new playback or three new starts. Evidence decays with a 14-day half-life. Legacy v0.2.x counters are preserved but excluded because channel errors could be misattributed.

fields.label: Use runtime reliability in sorting
fields.help_text: Reliability contributes at most +/-20 points inside the existing viability and resolution tiers. Streams without enough new evidence remain neutral.

fields.label: Files
fields.description: Unified analysis/throughput cache: /data/dispatcharr_stream_sort_analysis.json | Analysis status: /data/dispatcharr_stream_sort_status.json | Schedule state: /data/dispatcharr_stream_sort_schedule_state.json | Health trend report: /data/dispatcharr_stream_sort_health_report.json | TTL recommendation report: /data/dispatcharr_stream_sort_ttl_recommendations.json | Runtime reliability telemetry: /data/dispatcharr_stream_sort_reliability.json | Dry-run/apply report: /data/dispatcharr_stream_sort_report.json. Health history uses a 90-day retention window. Reset actions never clear the schedule or plugin settings. The old standalone throughput cache is read only as a migration fallback.

actions.label: Analyze Streams
actions.description: Incrementally refresh only health/content, metadata, or throughput data that needs checking in the selected channel scope.

confirm.title: Analyze assigned streams?
confirm.message: Fresh cached data and newer Dispatcharr playback metadata are reused. Provider connections are opened only for components that need refreshing. It does not rename, move, create, or delete channels.

actions.label: Check Analysis Status
actions.description: Show the current phase and progress of the active analysis, or the outcome of the last analysis.

actions.label: Stop Current Scan
actions.description: Stop new probes, safely drain active probes, and release their exact provider reservations.

confirm.title: Stop the current scan?
confirm.message: No new probes will start. Already-running probes will finish or time out so Stream Sort can release only the provider reservations it owns.

actions.label: Health Report
actions.description: Show problematic streams, directional health transitions, dead-to-alive recovery evidence, time concentration, report age, and the complete latest report without changing streams or settings.

actions.label: Recommend TTLs
actions.description: Read a recent non-empty health report and produce read-only TTL and jitter recommendations. Confidence remains low until enough directional transitions and history have been collected.

actions.label: Reset Scan Statistics
actions.description: Clear scan caches, status, health reports, TTL recommendations, and the legacy migration cache while preserving runtime reliability and playback history. Reset is refused while any manual, scheduled, or direct scan owns the analyzer lease.

confirm.title: Reset Stream Sort scan statistics?
confirm.message: This permanently clears scan data and the legacy migration cache. Runtime reliability and playback history are retained. The schedule, plugin settings, channel order, and provider configuration are preserved.

actions.label: Reset All Statistics
actions.description: Clear scan evidence plus all runtime reliability and playback history. Reset is refused while any manual, scheduled, or direct scan owns the analyzer lease.

confirm.title: Reset all Stream Sort statistics?
confirm.message: This permanently clears scan data, the legacy migration cache, runtime reliability, and playback history. The schedule, plugin settings, channel order, and provider configuration are preserved.

actions.label: Dry Run
actions.description: Calculate the proposed order for the selected channel scope without changing ChannelStream.order.

actions.label: Sort Streams
actions.description: Apply the calculated order to streams already assigned to channels inside the selected scope.

confirm.title: Apply stream ordering?
confirm.message: This changes ChannelStream.order only for the selected channel scope. It does not add or remove streams.

actions.label: Analyze + Sort
actions.description: Incrementally refresh required health/content/metadata/throughput data, then apply stream ordering.

confirm.title: Analyze and sort streams?
confirm.message: This refreshes only data that needs checking and then changes ChannelStream.order. It does not rename, move, create, or delete channels.

actions.label: Save Schedule
actions.description: Enable or refresh the cron schedule. Every run loads the current saved UI analysis settings; changing a TTL, filter, or worker value does not require reapplying the schedule.

actions.label: Check Schedule
actions.description: Show schedule configuration and the final status of the latest scheduled analysis, including running, completed, failed, or skipped-busy.

confirm.title: Disable schedule?
confirm.message: Scheduled analysis runs will stop after this change.

actions.label: Runtime Reliability (automatic)
actions.description: Required Dispatcharr event subscription. Current Dispatcharr versions display every subscribed action; clicking this row is an informational no-op and never creates synthetic telemetry.
